name: launch-simple
about: The default launch film, 15-30 s: a product shown doing its thing in a world, through hero shots. One world per film (src/world.tsx: a graded photograph or a lit field with its key light, dealt with the direction, never cut, racking soft behind the type), three or more hero shots dealt by the deck (src/hero: a glass input over the world as the camera pushes in while it types, the input at macro scale riding the caret, the page the product makes flown in and travelled, notifications stacking back in a blur ladder, a frosted composer focusing in, cards fanned in depth, a giant word with cards rising behind it, a porthole parting the line, a ring of real pictures, a push into the button as it is pressed, the 3D mark pulling back into the lockup), each filled with the product's own content (src/content.ts) and holding one sharp plane, one camera move that lands, light sized to its source; the creative elements (src/fx/creative) take the beats left. Lines centred and few, every change of picture carried, the lockup built from the last picture with the one fact under it. The agent writes the script (src/launch.ts), the content (scripts/content.mjs), the product's scenes (src/product.tsx) and fetches the world's plate; the timeline, the seams, the shots' moments, the end card and the sound plan follow. new-film.sh lays these files over the Remotion starter (the default for --format launch).

beats.T: a line alone, centred in the middle band, on a clean ground (launch.ts beat 'alone'; it builds over the last picture as that one falls back): 0.5-2.4 s (about 1.3), one entry voice for the film
beats.A: the product or the picture acting, full frame, centred, no statement over it: 1-3.5 s, varied (a long one beside a short one); a pair with no line is one A beat, carried on from the last picture
beats.TA: a line with its picture: the picture far behind it, centred, smaller, soft and dim, then coming up and racking into focus as the line leaves (beat 'with'), or the line held over a picture composed round it (beat 'over'): at most 40 % of the beats
beats.end: the centred lockup built from the last picture's element, the one fact under it, held 2-3 s
beats.mix: unset, the first line and the claim alone, the lines between with; aim for about T 25 % / T+A 30 % / A 37 % (timeline.ts BEAT_MIX): one 'over' in a film of four or five lines gets there

deal.seed: the deck's direction the agent picked (deck.py --direction <id> --why: it writes src/dealt.ts, one source), else the product's name (IDENTITY.name) or launch.ts seed; launch.ts pin fixes a slot by hand
deal.print: npx tsx -e "import { DEAL, DEAL_SOURCE, HERO_DEAL } from './src/deal'; import { HERO_PLAN, HERO_END, CREATIVE_PLAN, SEAM_PLAN, BEAT_PLAN } from './src/timeline'; console.log(DEAL_SOURCE, DEAL, HERO_DEAL.deal, HERO_PLAN, HERO_END, CREATIVE_PLAN, SEAM_PLAN.map((s) => s.recipe), BEAT_PLAN.map((b) => b.kind + ' ' + ((b.to - b.from) / 30).toFixed(2)))"

slots.creative: two or three of src/fx/creative (deal.ts CREATIVE: scripts/deck.py writes them into src/dealt.ts, else the name deals them), never a recent film's set; timeline.ts CREATIVE_PLAN puts them on at least half the beats
slots.hero: three or more of src/hero (deal.ts HERO_META), dealt by scripts/deck.py with the direction (the brief's words, the world's tone, the photos, the brand's mark) into src/dealt.ts hero, never the last film's set; timeline.ts HERO_PLAN puts them on their beats before the creative elements; a pair's `hero` pins one, launch.ts heroes.swap trades one with a reason

music.about: Every launch is cut to a licensed, human-made, instrumental track (references/music.md): the track carries the film and its cuts, earshot effects mark the picture's own moments (each line whole, the product's clicks and results, the seams that move, one hit on the lockup); never effects only. Any tempo from 90 to 140 BPM fits: the timeline fits each line and picture to the track's beats and each pair to whole bars.
music.pick: node scripts/music.mjs pick --mood "<the film's mood words>" --length <s> (a launch here: 115-136 BPM and the film's energy preferred; the curated library; with none, music.mjs search --bpm 115-136), then music.mjs get '#n' --to audio/music (its licence record beside it; never the last film's track)
music.add: bash scripts/new-film.sh <dir> --music <file> --title T --artist A --source S --page URL --licence L --seen-quote Q --seen-url URL --ai-generated no --vocals no, or later: python3 scripts/audio/track.py add <file> ...
then: python3 scripts/audio/track.py fit   (after launch.ts is written: the film's bars, the lockup's bar and the cuts read from the timeline at the track's tempo; the edit plays exactly those bars, lands the entry on the lockup, keeps sections from changing mid-shot, ends on a hit; then src/music.ts)
npm run music fits again after a change to the script or the track

next: simple launch: write the script in src/launch.ts (3-5 pairs: a line of 2-7 words and the picture that proves it; line 1 says what the product does by name; at most four lines; the one fact for the end card) and the name in src/brand/identity.ts,

deal: run deck.py here (three directions into out/OPTIONS.md, each with its world and hero shots), pick the one that fits the product and deal it with --direction <id> --why "<one line>" (src/dealt.ts: the world, the hero shots, the creative elements, the type pairing),

the world: a plate world (clouds, sky, aerial, sea, nightCity, studio, macro) needs its photograph: node scripts/assets.mjs plate <kind>, look at the sheet, then --pick <n> --to public/plates --accent '<accent>' (a built world needs nothing),

the content: node scripts/content.mjs --brief BRIEF.md --fetch --force (the request, the page, the notifications, the faces, the pictures the hero shots show), then read src/content.ts and keep only what is true of the product,

build each picture the hero shots leave in src/product.tsx from the product's real screens (each with its focus box, the one a push-press shot presses with its `button`, the last with its hero element); print the plan (template.json deal.print) and pin a shot to a pair (`hero`) where the story wants it there,
the mark: scripts/brand.py with the brand's SVG (or an invented brand's own mark) makes logo-3d dealable for the end card,
then the music (below), npm run check, the draft (render.sh --draft) and a contact sheet against references/checks.md
